recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It preserves the applied non-substantive clarification, removes a misleading cross-reference, and keeps the mapping exception synchronized with the resource definition; no further FHIR-7173 work is needed unless OO wants a broader cross-resource identifier policy change.
issue_request: FHIR-7173 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked that NutritionOrder.identifier relate to the filler and placer order concepts from HL7 V2 as signposts for readers, with the resolution saying to note that Identifier.type can indicate filler vs. placer if needed.
initial_application: Commit 534862556c ([#7177],[#7173]) initially added a NutritionOrder.identifier comment saying Identifier.type could indicate filler vs placer and linked to the then-current DiagnosticOrder notes. Later refactors carried that note into source/nutritionorder/structuredefinition-NutritionOrder.xml and commit 086649a235 added the matching Request mapping exception.
additional_context: NutritionOrder is active in source/fhir.ini, while the historical NutritionRequest name now appears only in the deleted-resource list. The carried-forward comment preserved the intended filler/placer note, but it had a grammar defect and pointed to servicerequest.html#notes for further detail even though the ServiceRequest notes section does not contain a filler/placer identifier discussion. Community searches found no direct FHIR-7173/Zulip/Confluence evidence that changed the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Updated source/nutritionorder/structuredefinition-NutritionOrder.xml and the matching source/nutritionorder/nutritionorder-request-mapping-exceptions.xml resource value to state directly: "The Identifier.type element can be used to indicate the HL7 V2 placer or filler order identifier if needed."
